\par\smallskip
\begin{tablenotes}
Share of the clean sample for which $w>1$ is identified beyond the designs (Proposition~\ref{prop:A-pi}(iii), (vii) and (viii)): $\ln M$ exceeds the upper end of the identified set for $\ln M^*(C)$ at the model's compute by at least $\ln\tau$; no model is identified as $w<1$ in any row. Tilt allowances $\tau$: 1.3, tokenizer differences; 1.84, the largest tilt across DataDecide's recipes, 0.26, which corresponds to $\tau\approx1.8$ under the reference exponents (we use 1.84); 3.4, the same tilt under DataDecide's own exponents; 4.4, both 1.3 and 3.4; Figure~\ref{fig:app-breakdown} traces $\tau$ up to 20. \textit{Primary:} one path per study, a line through the logged IsoFLOP minima at its bracketed budgets, extrapolated with a simultaneous 95 percent band for its level and slope (wild bootstrap-$t$, Webb weights, 9,999 draws, within-study pooled residual variance, critical value at least the normal-theory one) over $4.8\times10^{20}$ (Marin: from $3\times10^{20}$) to $4.0\times10^{25}$ FLOP; brackets give pointwise 95 percent intervals. Chinchilla: 9 budgets to $3\times10^{21}$ FLOP, total parameters as digitized (the convention of the models' $M$), level 20.7 [13.8, 30.9] at $3\times10^{21}$ FLOP, slope $-0.003$ $[-0.122,0.115]$. Llama~3: 8 budgets to $10^{21}$, FLOP-implied $N_F=C/(6D)$, level 15.1 [11.2, 20.3], slope $0.008$ $[-0.086,0.102]$. Marin: DCLM and Nemotron-CC (7 budgets each) and Comma (5) to $3\times10^{20}$, FLOP-implied, corpus levels 15.0, 15.5 and 20.8 and one slope, $0.198$ $[0.132,0.265]$, with a pooled residual variance (15 degrees of freedom). DeepSeek's published law enters as a point path in its own convention. The identified set is the union of the bands widened by $\ln\tau$; for $M^*(10^{24})$ it is [5.7, 248] and for $M^*(10^{25})$ [4.5, 468]. \textit{PI-1} (version 3): bootstrap-$t$ intervals for each design's level, slopes bounded by the point estimates of the paths and published laws, $[-0.156,0.162]$; Marin Comma (five budgets, interval $[0.2,3{,}586]$) was excluded by a rule of at least six budgets chosen after that interval was seen. \textit{$t$-interval levels:} levels on $t$-intervals with $k-2$ degrees of freedom, Comma admitted with its own slope, $0.294$; slopes in $[-0.156,0.294]$. \textit{Slopes at 95 percent intervals:} PI-1's levels, slopes in $[-0.175,0.353]$. \textit{Normal inputs only:} the primary levels, $|e|\le1$. \textit{Every technology:} the primary bands plus every in-set technology's in-support $M^*$, slopes in $[-0.131,0.311]$. \textit{Conventions:} models' $M$ is in total parameters except in the rows in FLOP-effective parameters. In total parameters, Marin's minima are converted with its measured ratio of FLOP-implied to configuration parameters (1.03 to 1.05 at the anchors), and Llama~3's band is shifted by the range of $\ln(N_F/N)$ at its anchor over three FLOP accountings, $[-0.25,0.20]$. In FLOP-effective parameters, Chinchilla's minima and the models' parameters follow Hoffmann et al.'s count (attention at 4,096 tokens for the models). Compute-weighted: shares of training compute $6ND$. Allocation decisions: members of one family that share one token budget (within 10 percent) form one decision; a decision is identified only if every member is.
\end{tablenotes}
